title: Optimistic Dual Averaging Unifies Modern Optimizers
claim: A baseline optimizer needs its hyperparameter swept to approach performance that our wrapper reaches untuned, and our wrapper still beats the best sweep.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, left-to-right, dashed horizontal line marks ours
description: Two side-by-side line charts share the same axes: weight decay from 0.0 to 1.0 on the x-axis and validation loss on the y-axis. The left panel is the shorter training horizon, 1x Chinchilla steps. The right panel is the longer horizon, 4x Chinchilla steps. In each panel an orange line with circular markers shows Muon at each swept weight decay. A flat black dashed horizontal line shows SODA(Muon), which needs no sweep. A legend in the top right names both series. On the left, the Muon loss falls steadily as weight decay rises but never reaches the dashed line. On the right, the Muon curve is U-shaped with a minimum near 0.3 to 0.5, and it also stays above the dashed line. The eye goes first to the gap between the orange curve and the black dashed baseline.
caption: Muon with swept weight decay is outperformed by SODA(Muon), without any additional tuning, on 124M models trained for both 1× Chinchilla steps (left) and 4× Chinchilla steps (right).
abstract: We introduce SODA, a generalization of Optimistic Dual Averaging, which provides a common perspective on state-of-the-art optimizers like Muon, Lion, AdEMAMix and NAdam, showing that they can all be viewed as optimistic instances of this framework. Based on this framing, we propose a practical SODA wrapper for any base optimizer that eliminates weight decay tuning through a theoretically-grounded $1/k$ decay schedule. Empirical results across various scales and training horizons show that SODA consistently improves performance without any additional hyperparameter tuning.
